verses.zh: （亚萨的训诲诗。）我的民哪，你们要留心听我的训诲，侧耳听我口中的话。
verses.en: A well-written song[NOTE:1] by Asaph.Pay attention, my people, to my instruction.Listen to the words I speak.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 78. The author of this lengthy didactic psalm rehearses Israel’s history. He praises God for his power, goodness and patience, but also reminds his audience that sin angers God and prompts his judgment. In the conclusion to the psalm the author elevates Jerusalem as God’s chosen city and David as his chosen king.
The meaning of the Hebrew term מַשְׂכִּיל (maskil) is uncertain. See the note on the phrase “well-written song” in the superscription of Ps 74.
verses.commentary:
78:1-4 The psalmist implores the covenant people to hear and respond appropriately to
God's revelation (cf. Ps. 78: 4c). He also implores them to pass on the truths to their children
and grandchildren and so on to each new generation (cf. Deut. 4:9-10; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 32:46).
Faith is only one generation away from unbelief!

78:1 There are two parallel IMPERATIVES.

- listen (lit. "hear") ‒ BDB 24, KB 27, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- incline your ears (lit. "turn") ‒ BDB 639, KB 692, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

▣ "instruction" This is literally "teaching" (BDB 435). This is parallel to "the words
of my mouth." There are several different Hebrew words used in this Psalm for YHWH's revelation.

- instruction/teaching, Ps. 78:1 - BDB 435

- testimony, Ps. 78:5 ‒ BDB 730

- law, Ps. 78:5,10 ‒ BDB 435

- commandment, Ps. 78:7 ‒ BDB 846

- testimonies, Ps. 78:56 ‒ BDB 729 I

This Psalm is written to the covenant people (usually the Psalms are addressed to God). It
seems this historical survey was used (read) in an annual feast or ceremony at the temple to encourage
God's people to learn from the past and live appropriately as God's people.

verses.zh: 我要开口说比喻；我要说出古时的谜语，
verses.en: I will sing a song that imparts wisdom;I will make insightful observations about the past.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Turn your ear to the words of my mouth.”
verses.commentary:
78:2 "parable. . .dark sayings"

- parable ‒ BDB 605

- dark saying ‒ BDB 295

The VERB and NOUN forms of both these words are found
in Ezek. 17:2. I have included my notes from there below.

Ezek. 17:2 This verse has two parallel IMPERATIVES.

- "propound a riddle," BDB 295, KB 295, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Jdgs. 14:12-19

- "speak a parable," BDB 605 II, KB 647, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. 12:23; 16:44;
17:2; 18:2; 20:49; 24:3

The term "riddle" (BDB 295, note the relation of the VERB, BDB 295, and
NOUN, BDB 295) means a statement that needs to have some information hinted at or
supplied to be understood (cf. Prov. 1:6).

The term "parable" (BDB 605 II, note the relation of the VERB, BDB 605 II,
and NOUN, BDB 605 II) implies a brief poetic structure, possibly a proverb which uses
comparison as a way to illustrate truth.

Ezekiel has been using highly figurative language to convince the exiles of the
just and sure judgment of Jerusalem.

YHWH is not trying to hide truth but assert that the key to understanding comes
from His speakers/prophets. The past acts of God need to be interpreted fresh for every generation.

Jesus quotes this verse in Matt. 13:35. He uses it to explain why the crowds did not
understand His teachings. He, too, reinterpreted Israel's past. He asserted that the ultimate focus
of Israel's history was Himself! However, this amazing truth was not immediately self evident but had
to be revealed! He was the true, ultimate revealer (cf. Matt. 5:17-19,21-48)! As Israel refused to
see YHWH's will and purpose in her history, so too, Jesus' generation lived out the prophecies of
Isa. 6:9-10; 29:13. They were like the Israelites of Ps. 78:8!

verses.zh: 是我们所听见、所知道的，也是我们的祖宗告诉我们的。
verses.en: What we have heard and learned[NOTE:1]—that which our ancestors[NOTE:2] have told us—
notes: Heb “I will open with a wise saying my mouth, I will utter insightful sayings from long ago.” Elsewhere the Hebrew word pair חִידָה + מָשָׁל (mashal + khidah) refers to a taunt song (Hab 2:6), a parable (Ezek 17:2), proverbial sayings (Prov 1:6), and an insightful song that reflects on the mortality of humankind and the ultimate inability of riches to prevent death (Ps 49:4).
Or “known.”

verses.zh: 我们不将这些事向他们的子孙隐瞒，要将耶和华的美德和他的能力，并他奇妙的作为，述说给后代听。
verses.en: we will not hide from their[NOTE:1] descendants.We will tell the next generationabout the Lord’s praiseworthy acts,[NOTE:2] about his strength and the amazing things he has done.
notes: Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 5, 8, 12, 57).
The pronominal suffix refers back to the “fathers” (“our ancestors,” v. 3).
verses.commentary:
78:4 Each generation must teach their children about God. This is a recurrent emphasis in
Deuteronomy. I have included my notes from Deut. 4:9 and 6:7.

Deut. 4:9 "teach their children" This is a recurrent theme in
Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:10; 6:7, 20-25; 11:19; 31:13; 32:46; and note
Exod. 10:2; 12:26; 13:8,14). If believers do not teach their children about
God, they are failures as parents (biblically speaking)! Faith runs through
families (cf. Deut. 5:10; 7:9)!

6:7 "you shall teach them diligently to your sons" The
VERB (BDB 1041, KB 1606, Piel PERFECT)
means "to sharpen" and in Piel this is the only usage. The term in
Ugaritic means "to repeat." That seems to be the basic emphasis of this verse.
The rabbis use this verse to assert that the Shema should be "repeated"
morning and evening. We are to talk about God's will for our lives during the
entire scope of daily activities. It is the responsibility of parents to pass
on lifestyle faith (cf. Deut. 4:9; 6:20-25; 11:19; 32:46, see full note at 4:9).
It is interesting that the flow of these different times for teaching falls
into the same literary pattern as Ps. 139:2-6 and Prov. 6:20-22. This emphasis
on parental responsibility is repeated in Prov. 22:6. Our modern day church school
cannot take the place of parental training but it surely can supplement it!

verses.zh: 因为，他在雅各中立法度，在以色列中设律法；是他吩咐我们祖宗要传给子孙的，
verses.en: He established a rule[NOTE:1] in Jacob;he set up a law in Israel.He commanded our ancestorsto make his deeds known to their descendants,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to a following generation telling the praises of the Lord.” “Praises” stand by metonymy for the mighty acts that prompt worship. Cf. Ps 9:14.
The Hebrew noun עֵדוּת (ʿedut) refers here to God’s command that the older generation teach their children about God’s mighty deeds in the nation’s history (see Exod 10:2; Deut 4:9; 6:20-25).
verses.commentary:
78:5-8 This strophe emphasizes the need for each generation of faithful followers to pass
on their faith and understanding of God's will to their families (see notes at Ps. 78:4).

Faithful followers are characterized as

- putting their confidence (lit. "hope," BDB 492) in God

- not forgetting His works, cf. Deut. 4:9,23; 31:6:12; 8:11,14,19 (twice); 9:7; 25:19

- keeping His commandments, cf. Deut. 4:2,6,10; 5:1,10,29,32; 6:2,3,17,25; 7:9,11,12;
27:1; Josh. 22:5

Psalm 78:7 is the positive theme of the entire Psalm while Ps. 78:8 is a powerful warning of
what not to do!

verses.zh: 使将要生的后代子孙可以晓得；他们也要起来告诉他们的子孙，
verses.en: so that the next generation, children yet to be born,might know about them.They will grow up and tell their descendants about them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “which he commanded our fathers to make them known to their sons.” The plural suffix “them” probably refers back to the Lord’s mighty deeds (see vv. 3-4).

verses.zh: 好叫他们仰望　神，不忘记　神的作为，惟要守他的命令。
verses.en: Then they will place their confidence in God.They will not forget the works of God,and they will obey[NOTE:1] his commands.
notes: Heb “in order that they might know, a following generation, sons [who] will be born, they will arise and will tell to their sons.”
verses.commentary:
78:7 "the works of God" This would involve the revelatory information of Genesis through Deuteronomy.

The name/title for Deity here is El (cf. v. 19), the general name for god in the ANE. In the
previous line of poetry, the title Elohim is used. Obviously, these two titles are related.

verses.zh: 不要像他们的祖宗，是顽梗悖逆、居心不正之辈，向着　神，心不诚实。
verses.en: Then they will not be like their ancestors,who were a stubborn and rebellious generation,a generation that was not committedand faithful to God.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “keep.”
verses.commentary:

verses.zh: 以法莲的子孙带着兵器，拿着弓，临阵之日转身退后。
verses.en: The Ephraimites[NOTE:1] were armed with bows,[NOTE:2] but they retreated in the day of battle.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “a generation that did not make firm its heart and whose spirit was not faithful with God.” The expression “make firm the heart” means “to be committed, devoted” (see 1 Sam 7:3).
Heb “the sons of Ephraim.” Ephraim probably stands here by synecdoche (part for whole) for the northern kingdom of Israel.

Heb “ones armed, shooters of bow.” It is possible that the term נוֹשְׁקֵי (nosheqey, “ones armed [with]”) is an interpretive gloss for the rare רוֹמֵי (rome, “shooters of”; on the latter see BDB 941 s.v. I רָמָה). The phrase נוֹשְׁקֵי קֶשֶׁת (nosheqe qeshet, “ones armed with a bow”) appears in 1 Chr 12:2; 2 Chr 17:17.
verses.commentary:
78:9-16 This strophe alludes to the Exodus. Some of the allusions are unclear (i.e., Ps. 78:9),
but many are (Contextual Insights, C) very clear.

Ephraim may be a way of referring to the Northern Tribes. Joseph and Joshua were both
from the tribe of Ephraim, which numerically was the largest tribe. Ephraim and Manasseh were both
sons of Joseph by an Egyptian mother. Jacob blessed Ephraim above the firstborn Manasseh
(cf. Gen. 48:14-20).

78:9 The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1368, asserts that many Jewish scholars (i.e., Rashi, Radak) think
this relates to Num. 14:39-45. They think Ephraimites instigated this disobedient attack.

The NET Bible, p. 948, thinks Ephraim is imagery referring to all the northern ten tribes, and
therefore, this would refer to Assyria's invasion.

verses.zh: 他们不遵守　神的约，不肯照他的律法行；
verses.en: They did not keep their covenant with God,[NOTE:1] and they refused to obey[NOTE:2] his law.
notes: They retreated. This could refer to the northern tribes’ failure to conquer completely their allotted territory (see Judg 1), or it could refer generally to the typical consequence (military defeat) of their sin (see vv. 10-11).
Heb “the covenant of God.”
verses.commentary:
78:10 Note the VERBS "keep" (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT,
negated) and "walk" (BDB 229, KB 246) are parallel and describe covenant life. Obedience to the Mosaic
covenant was crucial (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-30).

verses.zh: 又忘记他所行的和他显给他们奇妙的作为。
verses.en: They forgot what he had done,[NOTE:1] the amazing things he had shown them.
notes: Heb “walk in.”
verses.commentary:
78:11 That generation of the Israelites forgot all that YHWH had done for them during
the exodus (cf. Deut. 8:11-20). So in the verses that follow many of YHWH's mighty acts of deliverance
are enumerated.

verses.zh: 他在埃及地，在琐安田，在他们祖宗的眼前施行奇事。
verses.en: He did amazing things in the sight of their ancestors,in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his deeds.”
verses.commentary:
78:12 "Zoan" This term (BDB 858) is from an Egyptian root for "stronghold." This stronghold/fort
was located in the Delta region of Egypt, also known as Goshen (eastern Nile Delta), where the
Israelites settled in Joseph's day. The city was known by different names in different periods.

- Zoan (cf. Num. 13:22)

- Tannis

- Avaris

- Rameses (named after Rameses II, cf. Exod. 1:11; 12:37; Num. 33:3)

verses.zh: 他将海分裂，使他们过去，又叫水立起如垒。
verses.en: He divided the sea and led them across it;he made the water stand in a heap.
verses.commentary: 78:13 "divided the sea" See Exodus 14.

verses.zh: 他白日用云彩，终夜用火光引导他们。
verses.en: He led them with a cloud by dayand with the light of a fire all night long.

verses.zh: 他在旷野分裂磐石，多多地给他们水喝，如从深渊而出。
verses.en: He broke open rocks in the wildernessand gave them enough water to fill the depths of the sea.[NOTE:1]
notes: The region of Zoan was located in the Egyptian delta, where the enslaved Israelites lived (see Num 13:22; Isa 19:11, 13; 30:4; Ezek 30:14).
verses.commentary: 78:15-16 "split the rocks" See Exodus 17.

verses.zh: 他使水从磐石涌出，叫水如江河下流。
verses.en: He caused streams to flow from the rockand made the water flow like rivers.

verses.zh: 他们却仍旧得罪他，在干燥之地悖逆至高者。
verses.en: Yet they continued to sin against himand rebelled against the Most High[NOTE:1] in the desert.
notes: Heb “and caused them to drink, like the depths, abundantly.”
verses.commentary:
78:17-20 This strophe continues to describe the acts of the ungrateful, disobedient
Israelites of the exodus and wilderness wandering period.

verses.zh: 他们心中试探　神，随自己所欲的求食物，
verses.en: They willfully challenged God[NOTE:1] by asking for food to satisfy their appetite.
notes: The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן ʿelyon) pictures God as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked. See especially Pss 7:17; 9:2; 18:13; 21:7; 47:2.

IMPERFECT with waw) is used several times of Israel testing God
(cf. Exod. 17:2; Num. 14:22; Deut. 6:16; Ps. 78:18,41,56; 95:9; 106:14).

verses.zh: 并且妄论　神说：　神在旷野岂能摆设筵席吗？
verses.en: They insulted God, saying,[NOTE:1] “Is God really able to give us food[NOTE:2] in the wilderness?
notes: Heb “and they tested God in their heart.” The “heart” is viewed here as the center of their volition.
Heb “they spoke against God, they said.”

verses.zh: 他曾击打磐石，使水涌出，成了江河；他还能赐粮食吗？还能为他的百姓预备肉吗？
verses.en: Yes,[NOTE:1] he struck a rock and water flowed out;streams gushed forth.But can he also give us food?Will he provide meat for his people?”
notes: Heb “to arrange a table [for food].”

verses.zh: 所以，耶和华听见就发怒；有烈火向雅各烧起；有怒气向以色列上腾；
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] the Lord heard this, he was furious.A fire broke out against Jacob,and his anger flared up[NOTE:2] against Israel,
notes: Heb “look.”
Heb “therefore.”
verses.commentary:
78:21-33 Israel's continued disobedience causes YHWH to judge them (i.e., fire, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE). One example of God's faithful love and Israel's disobedience is
YHWH's supernatural provisions of meat (quail). He told them how to receive His blessing but again
they disobeyed (cf. Numbers 11). Their actions showed their attitude toward YHWH.

- they did not believe, Ps. 78:22 (BDB 52, KB 63, Hiphil PERFECT)

- they did not trust, Ps. 78:22 (BDB 105, KB 120, Qal PERFECT)

- in spite of all this they still sinned, Ps. 78:32

verses.zh: 因为他们不信服　神，不倚赖他的救恩。
verses.en: because they did not have faith in Godand did not trust his ability to deliver them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and also anger went up.”

verses.zh: 他却吩咐天空，又敞开天上的门，
verses.en: He gave a command to the clouds aboveand opened the doors in the sky.
verses.commentary:
78:23 "opened the doors of heaven" The "heavens" (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN and
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN AND THE
THIRD HEAVEN) were thought of as a dome covered with skin, like a drum. This dome separated
the waters above from falling to earth. They were imagined to have windows that could be opened
or shut, depending on God's will and mankind's actions (cf. Gen. 7:11; Mal. 3:10). God could provide

- rain (Genesis)

- food (Psalm)

- blessings (Malachi)

verses.zh: 降吗哪，像雨给他们吃，将天上的粮食赐给他们。
verses.en: He rained down manna for them to eat;he gave them the grain of heaven.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they did not trust his deliverance.”
verses.commentary:
78:24-25 "food from heaven. . .the bread of angels" This is referring to manna (cf. Exodus 16).
YHWH was gracious (cf. Ps. 78:38), but they were rebellious (cf. Exodus 16).

Manna (BDB 577 I) was a white substance that appeared as dew. The name may come from
Exod. 16:15, "What is it?" It was a miraculous provision of food during the wilderness wandering
period. It could be gathered for only one day at a time (God's daily provision) or it went bad
(cf. Exod. 16:16-21), except for the day before the Sabbath when enough for two days was gathered
and did not turn bad (cf. Exod. 16:22-29). It was cooked like flour. It stopped when the Israelites
crossed the Jordan (cf. Josh. 5:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MANNA

verses.zh: 各人（或译：人）吃大能者的食物；他赐下粮食，使他们饱足。
verses.en: Man ate the food of the mighty ones.[NOTE:1] He sent them more than enough to eat.[NOTE:2]
notes: Manna was apparently shaped like a seed (Exod 16:31), perhaps explaining why it is here compared to grain.

Because of the reference to “heaven” in the preceding verse, it is likely that mighty ones refers here to the angels of heaven. The LXX translates “angels” here, as do a number of modern translations (NEB, NIV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
78:25

NASB, REV, NRSV, LXX
"the bread of angels"

NKJV, Peshitta
"angel's food"

NJB
"the bread of the Mighty"

JPSOA
"a hero's meal"

NET
"the food of the mighty ones"

The MT has the PLURAL ADJECTIVE "mighty ones" or "valiant ones"
(BDB 7, KB 6). It is used of

- humans

- violent ‒ Job 24:32

- mighty, wealthy ‒ Job 34:20

- stubborn ‒ Isa. 46:12

- strong ‒ Isa. 10:13

- angels ‒ Ps. 103:20; possibly Ps. 29:1; 78:25

- animals

- bulls ‒ Ps. 22:12; 51:13; 68:30; Isa. 1:24; 10:3; 34:7; Jer. 46:15

- horses ‒ Jdg. 5:22; Jer. 8;16; 47:3; 50:11

- obviosly it is used as imagery for enemies

It seems that the usage here is parallel to "grain from heaven" in v. 24, and therefore, refers
to angels. This is surprising since no where else do angels eat like humans.

verses.zh: 他领东风起在天空，又用能力引了南风来。
verses.en: He brought the east wind through the skyand by his strength led forth the south wind.

verses.zh: 他降肉，像雨在他们当中，多如尘土，又降飞鸟，多如海沙，
verses.en: He rained down meat on them like dust,birds as numerous as the sand on the seashores.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “provision he sent to them to satisfaction.”
verses.commentary:
78:27 "dust. . .sand" These are two of three terms (dust, sand, stars) used to describe
something numerous. They are regularly connected to the numerous descendants of the Patriarchs
(i.e., God's promise to Abraham, cf. Gen. 12:2).

- dust ‒ Gen. 13:16; 28:14; Num. 23:10

- sand ‒ Gen. 22:17; 32:12; 2 Sam. 17:11; 1 Kgs. 4:20

- stars ‒ Gen. 15:5; 22:17; 26:4; Exod. 32:13; Deut. 1:10; 10:22; 28:62

verses.zh: 落在他们的营中，在他们住处的四面。
verses.en: He caused them to fall right in the middle of their camp,all around their homes.

verses.zh: 他们吃了，而且饱足；这样就随了他们所欲的。
verses.en: They ate until they were beyond full;[NOTE:1] he gave them what they desired.
notes: Heb “and like the sand of the seas winged birds.”
verses.commentary:
78:29-31 God provided quail but the people again did not trust God's provision and tried
to gather a large quantity of birds for future consumption. This displeased God and His judgment
fell on them (cf. Num. 11:31-35).

Again and again in the OT, God told His people what to do but they refused and did
it their way. Every time this resulted in judgment! The issue was "trust"! And it still is!

verses.zh: 他们贪而无厌，食物还在他们口中的时候，
verses.en: They were not yet filled up;[NOTE:1] their food was still in their mouths
notes: Heb “and they ate and were extremely filled.” The verb שָׂבַע (savaʿ, “be satisfied, full”) is often used of eating and/or drinking one’s fill, to have had fully enough and want no more. See BDB 959 s.v. שָׂבַע. In some cases it means to have had more than enough of something (cf. Prov 25:17; Isa 1:11). Here the use of מְאֹד (meʾod, “very”) and the context of the account indicate they felt filled beyond capacity.

verses.zh: 神的怒气就向他们上腾，杀了他们内中的肥壮人，打倒以色列的少年人。
verses.en: when the anger of God flared up against them.He killed some of the strongest of them;he brought the young men of Israel to their knees.

verses.zh: 虽是这样，他们仍旧犯罪，不信他奇妙的作为。
verses.en: Despite all this, they continued to sin,and did not trust him to do amazing things.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “they were not separated from their desire.”

verses.zh: 因此，他叫他们的日子全归虚空，叫他们的年岁尽属惊恐。
verses.en: So he caused them to die unsatisfied[NOTE:1] and filled with terror.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and did not believe in his amazing deeds.”
Heb “and he ended in vanity their days.”
verses.commentary:
78:33

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA
"end in futility"

NASB margin
"vanity, a mere breath"

NRSV
"vanish like a breath"

NJB
"vanish in mist"

LXX
"in vanity"

Peshitta, REB
"in emptiness"

This term (BDB 210 I) is a key term in Ecclesiastes. See my note below from
Ecclesiastes 1.

Eccl. 1:2 "vanity of vanities" This is a Hebrew
superlative (cf. 1:2 and 12:8). The word means "vapor," "breath," or
"mist" (BDB 210 I, cf. James 4:14). Its emphasis is either

- nothingness

- the transitoriness of human life

The context supports the latter (cf. H. C. Leupold, Exposition
of Ecclesiastes, p. 41).

This is a key term and recurrent phrase in this book
(cf. Eccl. 1:2,14; 2:1,11,15,17,19,21, 23,26; 3:19; 4:4,7,8,16; 5:7,10;
6:2,4,9,11,12; 7:6,15; 8:10,14; 9:9; 11:8,10; 12:8). The term is used
sparingly in other wisdom books: Job, 5 times; Psalms, 9 times; and Proverbs, 3 times.

For different theories about how it views the strong
statements in this book, see Introduction, Authorship, H. I prefer option #1.
This theological presupposition will be the grid through which I interpret the book.

▣ "all is vanity" Notice the root, "vanity" (BDB 210 I), is used
five times in this one verse! The Handbook on Ecclesiastes by UBS, says
the term should be understood as

- incomprehensible

- enigmatic

- mysterious

- impossible to understand

Therefore, it communicates the reality that life is full of
unanswerable questions (p. 4). The person knowledgeable in wisdom will know this,
but will continue to trust God and keep His commandments.

This refers to the uncertain and unpredictable activities of
life. These are a result of fallen humanity trying to live life in their own
strength, independent from God. This is the condition left by the Fall (cf. Genesis 3)!

The Hebrew term "all" (BDB 481), often translated "everything,"
is a common word, but is used often in Ecclesiastes (i.e., 9 times in chapter 1;
17 times in chapter 2; 13 times in chapter 3, etc.). Qoheleth uses this
inclusive language to express his theological emphasis on

- God's control and sovereignty

- human ineffectiveness and transitoriness

verses.zh: 他杀他们的时候，他们才求问他，回心转意，切切地寻求　神。
verses.en: When he struck them down,[NOTE:1] they sought his favor;[NOTE:2] they turned back and longed for God.
notes: Heb “and their years in terror.”
Or “killed them,” that is, killed large numbers of them.
verses.commentary:
78:34-39 This strophe describes the false repentance of the surviving Israelites and
YHWH's reaction to it.

- the seeming repentance, Ps. 78:34-35

- they sought Him

- they returned to Him

- they searched diligently for Him

- they remembered God was their rock/redeemer

- their true thoughts/actions (Ps. 78:36-37)

- they deceived Him by lying (Ps. 78:36 a and b, cf. Isa. 29:13)

- their hearts were not steadfast toward Him

- they were not faithful to His covenant

- YHWH's reactions (Ps. 78:38-39)

- He is compassionate (cf. Exod. 34:6; Neh. 9:17; Ps. 103:8, see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD)

- He forgave (lit. "covered over," BDB 497, KB 493, Piel IMPERFECT)

- He did not destroy them

- He restrained (lit. "turned away") His anger

- He did not arouse all His wrath

- He remembered that they were but flesh (cf. Gen. 3:19; Ps. 103:14) which is here today and gone tomorrow

Psalm 78:38-39 does not mean that they were not judged (cf. Ps. 78:34a), but
that YHWH did not completely destroy them.

Psalm 78:38-39 is used in many rabbinical writings. It is a summary of the
character of God (cf. Exod. 34:6; Neh. 9:17; Ps. 103:8-14).

verses.zh: 他们也追念　神是他们的磐石，至高的　神是他们的救赎主。
verses.en: They remembered that God was their protector[NOTE:1] and that God Most High[NOTE:2] was their deliverer.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “they sought him.”
Heb “my high rocky summit.”
The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן ʿelyon) pictures God as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked. See especially Pss 7:17; 9:2; 18:13; 21:7; 47:2.
verses.commentary:
78:35 Notice the different names and titles for Deity (see Contextual Insights, E.).

- Elohim (BDB 43, KB 52)

- their rock (cf. Ps. 18:2; 19:14)

- El (BDB 42, KB 48)

- Elyon (BDB 751, KB 832)

- their redeemer (cf. Ps. 19:14)

▣ "their rock" See Deut. 32:3-4 for a good understanding of this title (also note Ps. 18:1-3).

▣ "their redeemer" For this title see
SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM. It has family implications.

verses.zh: 他们却用口谄媚他，用舌向他说谎。
verses.en: But they deceived him with their words[NOTE:1] and lied to him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “redeemer”
Heb “with their mouth.”

verses.zh: 因他们的心向他不正，在他的约上也不忠心。
verses.en: They were not really committed to him,[NOTE:1] and they were unfaithful to his covenant.
notes: Heb “and with their tongue they lied to him.”
verses.commentary:
78:37 "covenant" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 但他有怜悯，赦免他们的罪孽，不灭绝他们，而且屡次消他的怒气，不发尽他的忿怒。
verses.en: Yet he is compassionate.He forgives sin and does not destroy.He often holds back his angerand does not stir up his fury.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and their heart was not firm with him.”

verses.zh: 他想到他们不过是血气，是一阵去而不返的风。
verses.en: He remembered[NOTE:1] that they were made of fleshand were like a wind that blows past and does not return.[NOTE:2]
notes: One could translate v. 38 in the past tense (“he was compassionate…forgave sin and did not destroy…held back his anger, and did not stir up his fury”), but the imperfect verbal forms are probably best understood as generalizing. Verse 38 steps back briefly from the narrational summary of Israel’s history and lays the theological basis for v. 39, which focuses on God’s mercy toward sinful Israel.
The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive signals a return to the narrative.
verses.commentary: 78:39 This same imagery of the frailty and transitoriness of humankind is found in Ps. 103:15-16.

verses.zh: 他们在旷野悖逆他，在荒地叫他担忧，何其多呢！
verses.en: How often they rebelled against him in the wildernessand insulted him[NOTE:1] in the wastelands.
notes: Heb “and he remembered that they [were] flesh, a wind [that] goes and does not return.”
verses.commentary:
78:40-53 There seems to be a merging in this strophe between YHWH's judgment on
the Israelites (cf. Ps. 78:40-42) and His judgment on Egypt during the exodus. The plagues
alluded to in Ps. 78:43-51 were directed at the recalcitrant Egyptian leadership. Those plagues each
depreciated an Egyptian deity and showed YHWH's person and power!

Instead of YHWH judging faithless Israel (i.e., wilderness wandering period,
cf. Ps. 78:40-43), He was a shepherd to them (cf. Ps. 78:52-53).

Notice how Israel's faithlessness is characterized.

- they rebelled against Him, Ps. 78:40

- they grieved Him, Ps. 78:40

- they tempted Him, Ps. 78:41

- they pained Him, Ps. 78:41

- they did not remember His power/signs/marvels, Ps. 78:42

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

verses.zh: 他们再三试探　神，惹动以色列的圣者。
verses.en: They again challenged God[NOTE:1] and offended[NOTE:2] the Holy One of Israel.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “caused him pain.”
Heb “and they returned and tested God.” The Hebrew verb שׁוּב (shuv, “to return”) is used here in an adverbial sense to indicate that an earlier action was repeated.
Or “wounded, hurt.” The verb occurs only here in the OT.
verses.commentary:
78:41 "Holy One of Israel" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

▣ See Num. 14:22 which is a summary statement of the wilderness wandering period.

verses.zh: 他们不追念他的能力（原文是手）和赎他们脱离敌人的日子；
verses.en: They did not remember what he had done,[NOTE:1] how he delivered them from the enemy,[NOTE:2]
notes: The basic sense of the word “holy” is “set apart from that which is commonplace, special, unique.” The Lord’s holiness is first and foremost his transcendent sovereignty as the ruler of the world. He is “set apart” from the world over which he rules. At the same time his holiness encompasses his moral authority, which derives from his royal position. As king he has the right to dictate to his subjects how they are to live; indeed his very own character sets the standard for proper behavior. This expression is a common title for the Lord in the book of Isaiah.
Heb “his hand,” symbolizing his saving activity and strength, as the next line makes clear.

verses.zh: 他怎样在埃及地显神迹，在琐安田显奇事，
verses.en: when he performed his awesome deeds[NOTE:1] in Egyptand his acts of judgment[NOTE:2] in the region of Zoan.
notes: Heb “[the] day [in] which he ransomed them from [the] enemy.”
Or “signs” (see Ps 65:8).
verses.commentary:
78:43 "His signs in Egypt" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGNS (OT)

verses.zh: 把他们的江河并河汊的水都变为血，使他们不能喝。
verses.en: He turned their rivers into blood,and they could not drink from their streams.
verses.commentary:
78:44-51 These verses describe the plagues on Egypt.

- water/river to blood ‒ Exod. 7:17-19

- flies ‒ Exod. 8:16-18

- frogs ‒ Exod. 8:2-6

- grasshopper/locusts ‒ Exod. 8:21; 10:4-6

- hailstones ‒ Exod. 9:18

- plague/sickness ‒ Exod. 9:8-10

- death of firstborn ‒ Exodus 11

The order and number are not exact but obviously the ten plagues of Exodus
7-11 are what is being referred to, unless they became idioms of YHWH's judgment.

verses.zh: 他叫苍蝇成群落在他们当中，嘬尽他们，又叫青蛙灭了他们，
verses.en: He sent swarms of biting insects against them,[NOTE:1] as well as frogs that overran their land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “portents, omens” (see Ps 71:7). The Egyptian plagues are referred to here (see vv. 44-51).
Heb “and he sent an insect swarm against them and it devoured them.”

verses.zh: 把他们的土产交给蚂蚱，把他们辛苦得来的交给蝗虫。
verses.en: He gave their crops to the grasshopper,the fruit of their labor to the locust.

verses.zh: 他降冰雹打坏他们的葡萄树，下严霜打坏他们的桑树，
verses.en: He destroyed their vines with hailand their sycamore-fig trees with driving rain.
verses.commentary:
78:47 YHWH reverses His agricultural blessings (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-30). Now, they
received the prophetic curses.

verses.zh: 又把他们的牲畜交给冰雹，把他们的群畜交给闪电。
verses.en: He rained hail down on their cattle[NOTE:1] and hurled lightning bolts down on their livestock.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and a swarm of frogs and it destroyed them.”
Heb “and he turned over to the hail their cattle.”

verses.zh: 他使猛烈的怒气和忿怒、恼恨、苦难成了一群降灾的使者，临到他们。
verses.en: His raging anger lashed out against them.[NOTE:1] He sent fury, rage, and troubleas messengers who bring disaster.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and their livestock to the flames.” “Flames” here refer to the lightning bolts that accompanied the storm.

Heb “he sent against them the rage of his anger.” The phrase “rage of his anger” employs an appositional genitive. Synonyms are joined in a construct relationship to emphasize the single idea. For a detailed discussion of the grammatical point with numerous examples, see Y. Avishur, “Pairs of Synonymous Words in the Construct State (and in Appositional Hendiadys) in Biblical Hebrew,” Semitics 2 (1971): 17-81.
verses.commentary:
78:49 This verse uses a litany of terms to describe God's wrath (Ps. 78:38).

- burning anger ‒ BDB 354 CONSTRUCT BDB 60 I

- fury ‒ BDB 720

- indignation ‒ BDB 276

- trouble ‒ BDB 865

- a band of destroying angels

Number 5 is an idiom which personifies God's elements of wrath. In the Exodus
account of the death of the firstborn in the unmarked homes, it is God who Himself causes
the event (cf. Exod. 11:4; 12:12). This later became Judaism's understanding of "the Death
Angel" (i.e., Samael or Azrael), but the Bible does not specifically mention him, although
2 Sam. 24:16; 2 Kgs. 19:35; 1 Chr. 21:15; Isa. 37:36, do imply one. The rabbis also assert
that Ps. 89:48 refers to him (i.e., Targum, "seeing the angel of death"). The theological
point is that God, not Satan or an angel, controls death!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ONE CAUSALAITY

verses.zh: 他为自己的怒气修平了路，将他们交给瘟疫，使他们死亡，
verses.en: He sent his anger in full force.[NOTE:1] He did not spare them from death;he handed their lives over to destruction.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “fury and indignation and trouble, a sending of messengers of disaster.”
Heb “he leveled a path for his anger.” There were no obstacles to impede its progress; it moved swiftly and destructively.
verses.commentary:
78:50 This is an idiom for the preparation for an action. The next two lines show that
in this case it was YHWH's judgment.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "soul" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

▣ "to the plague" This may be a personification parallel to "a band of destroying angels"
in the previous verse.

verses.zh: 在埃及击杀一切长子，在含的帐棚中击杀他们强壮时头生的。
verses.en: He struck down all the firstborn in Egypt,the firstfruits of their reproductive power[NOTE:1] in the tents of Ham.
notes: Or perhaps “[the] plague.”

verses.zh: 他却领出自己的民如羊，在旷野引他们如羊群。
verses.en: Yet he brought out his people like sheep;he led them through the wilderness like a flock.
verses.commentary: 78:52 God as shepherd is a recurrent theme in the Psalms of Asaph. See note at Ps. 77:20.

verses.zh: 他领他们稳稳妥妥地，使他们不致害怕；海却淹没他们的仇敌。
verses.en: He guided them safely along, and they were not afraid;but the sea covered their enemies.
verses.commentary:
78:53 This verse has two historical allusions.

- "led them" refers to the Shekinah cloud of glory that guided the Israelites
(cf. Exod. 13:21; 14:19,24; 33:9,10)

- "the sea engulfed their enemies" refers to the splitting of the Red Sea and then
its returning water drowning Egypt's elite soldiers and chariots (cf. Exodus 14-15)

verses.zh: 他带他们到自己圣地的边界，到他右手所得的这山地。
verses.en: He brought them to the border of his holy land,to this mountainous land[NOTE:1] that his right hand[NOTE:2] acquired.
notes: Heb “the beginning of strength.” If retained, the plural form אוֹנִים (ʾonim, “strength”) probably indicates degree (“great strength”), but many ancient witnesses read “their strength,” which presupposes an emendation to אֹנָם (ʾonam; singular form of the noun with third masculine plural pronominal suffix).
Heb “this mountain.” The whole land of Canaan seems to be referred to here. In Exod 15:17 the promised land is called the “mountain of your [i.e., God’s] inheritance.”
verses.commentary:
78:54-64 This strophe recounts the conquest and settlement of the Promised Land
(cf. Gen. 15:12-21). The Canaanite tribes (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE) were defeated and removed by God because of
their sin (cf. Gen. 15:12-21). Tragically the same thing happens to the Israelite tribes in the two exiles
(i.e., Assyria, Neo-Babylon).

78:54b This is anthropomorphic imagery asserting that the Conquest was by YHWH's hand, not Israeli
military power.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

78:55b The book of Joshua, chapters 12-19, describes the divine allotment of the land
to Jacob's children.

verses.zh: 他在他们面前赶出外邦人，用绳子将外邦的地量给他们为业，叫以色列支派的人住在他们的帐棚里。
verses.en: He drove the nations out from before them;he assigned them their tribal allotments[NOTE:1] and allowed the tribes of Israel to settle down.[NOTE:2]
notes: The “right hand” here symbolizes God’s military strength (see v. 55).
Heb “he caused to fall [to] them with a measuring line an inheritance.”

verses.zh: 他们仍旧试探、悖逆至高的　神，不守他的法度，
verses.en: Yet they challenged and defied[NOTE:1] God Most High[NOTE:2] and did not obey[NOTE:3] his commands.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and caused the tribes of Israel to settle down in their tents.”
Or “tested and rebelled against.”
The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן ʿelyon) pictures God as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked. See especially Pss 7:17; 9:2; 18:13; 21:7; 47:2.
Or “keep.”
verses.commentary:
78:56-58 These lines of poetry describe Israel's sin and rebellion, which is all the more
terrible because of all that God had done for them (cf. Luke 12:48).

- they tempted God, Ps. 78:56a

- they rebelled against God, Ps. 78:56a

- they did not keep His covenant, Ps. 78:56b

- they turned their backs to Him, Ps. 78:57a

- they acted treacherously as their fathers did, Ps. 78:57a

- they turned aside like a treacherous bow, Ps. 78:57b

- they provoked Him with Canaanite idolatry, Ps. 78:58a

- they aroused His jealousy with graven images, Ps. 78:58b

78:56 "the Most High God" This title/name is a combination of Elyon and Elohim (cf. v. 35).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, B., C.

▣ "keep" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "testimonies" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

verses.zh: 反倒退后，行诡诈，像他们的祖宗一样；他们改变，如同翻背的弓。
verses.en: They were unfaithful[NOTE:1] and acted as treacherously as[NOTE:2] their ancestors;they were as unreliable as a malfunctioning bow.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his testimonies” (see Ps 25:10).
Heb “they turned back.”
Or “acted treacherously like.”

verses.zh: 因他们的邱坛惹了他的怒气；因他们雕刻的偶像触动他的愤恨。
verses.en: They made him angry with their pagan shrines[NOTE:1] and made him jealous with their idols.
notes: Heb “they turned aside like a deceitful bow.”
verses.commentary:
78:58 This describes the worship of Canaanite fertility gods on the "high places."

- Asherah ‒ a carved pole

- Ba'al ‒ a raised stone

verses.zh: 神听见就发怒，极其憎恶以色列人。
verses.en: God heard and was angry;he completely rejected Israel.
verses.commentary:
78:59-64 These verses describe what God did to Israel in light of their actions (Ps. 78:56-58).

- He was filled with wrath

- He greatly abhorred Israel

- He abandoned the dwelling place at Shiloh (cf. 1 Sam. 4:11)

- He allowed Israel to be defeated

- He delivered Israel to the sword

- He was filled with wrath at His inheritance

- fire devoured the young men (i.e., soldiers)

- the virgins had no wedding (i.e., no normal cultural events)

- the priests were killed (i.e., holy places violated)

- the widows could not weep (possibly the widows of the priests)

Human choices have consequences, both temporal and eternal!

verses.zh: 甚至他离弃示罗的帐幕，就是他在人间所搭的帐棚；
verses.en: He abandoned[NOTE:1] the sanctuary at Shiloh,the tent where he lived among men.
notes: Traditionally, “high places.”

verses.zh: 又将他的约柜（原文是能力）交与人掳去，将他的荣耀交在敌人手中；
verses.en: He allowed the symbol of his strong presence to be captured;[NOTE:1] he gave the symbol of his splendor[NOTE:2] into the hand of the enemy.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “rejected.”
Heb “and he gave to captivity his strength.” The expression “his strength” refers metonymically to the ark of the covenant, which was housed in the tabernacle at Shiloh.
Heb “and his splendor into the hand of an enemy.” The expression “his splendor” also refers metonymically to the ark of the covenant.
verses.commentary:
78:61 This verse seems to allude to the capturing of the Ark of the Covenant by the Philistines
in battle (cf. 1 Sam. 4:17). The OT never mentions lthe destruction of Shiloh, but it is assumed the
Philistines did it.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

verses.zh: 并将他的百姓交与刀剑，向他的产业发怒。
verses.en: He delivered his people over to the swordand was angry with his chosen nation.[NOTE:1]
notes: Verses 60-61 refer to the Philistines’ capture of the ark in the days of Eli (1 Sam 4:1-11).
verses.commentary:
78:62 "His inheritance" This is a parallel to "His people" (cf. Ps. 106:40). The origin
of this imagery is Deut. 9:29. It, like so many other images, is family oriented.

verses.zh: 少年人被火烧灭；处女也无喜歌。
verses.en: Fire consumed their[NOTE:1] young men,and their[NOTE:2] virgins remained unmarried.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his inheritance.”
Heb “his.” The singular pronominal suffix is collective, referring back to God’s “people” (v. 62).
Heb “his.” The singular pronominal suffix is collective, referring back to God’s “people” (v. 62).
verses.commentary:
78:63 "fire" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

verses.zh: 祭司倒在刀下，寡妇却不哀哭。
verses.en: Their[NOTE:1] priests fell by the sword,but their[NOTE:2] widows did not weep.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “were not praised,” that is, in wedding songs. The young men died in masses, leaving no husbands for the young women.
Heb “his.” The singular pronominal suffix is collective, referring back to God’s “people” (v. 62).
Heb “his.” The singular pronominal suffix is collective, referring back to God’s “people” (v. 62).

verses.zh: 那时，主像世人睡醒，像勇士饮酒呼喊。
verses.en: But then the Lord awoke from his sleep;[NOTE:1] he was like a warrior in a drunken rage.[NOTE:2]
notes: Because of the invading army and the ensuing panic, the priests’ widows had no time to carry out the normal mourning rites.
Heb “and the master awoke like one sleeping.” The Lord’s apparent inactivity during the time of judgment is compared to sleep.
verses.commentary:
78:65-72 This concluding strophe describes how God turned from wrath to continue His
redemptive purposes (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S
ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

- God is described as a person who comes to his senses (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (ANTHROPOMORPHISM))

- He defeats the adversaries of His people

- He gives them an everlasting reproach

- He reorients the order of the tribes as to places of leadership

- rejects Joseph and Ephraim

- chooses the tribe of Judah (cf. Gen. 49:8-12; Deut. 33:7)

- He chooses to locate the temple in Judah on Mt. Moriah (called Zion)

- He chooses David as His special leader (and his descendants, cf. 2 Samuel 7)

- described as a shepherd

- has a heart of integrity

- has skillful hands

With the allusion to God's rejection of the Northern Tribes and choice of Judah, it
seems this Psalm's final form was written after the fall of Israel/Ephraim/Samaria in
722 B.C. to Assyria.

This strophe is a good example of how God asserts His sovereignty. The cultural
expectation is altered to show God's control.

- Judah not Ephraim

- Zion not Shiloh

- David not other sons of Jesse

This is similar theologically to the Patriarchs all marrying barren women. Their
children were supernatural-natural gifts from God. He is in control of time, space, history,
election, and salvation!

verses.zh: 他就打退了他的敌人，叫他们永蒙羞辱；
verses.en: He drove his enemies back;he made them a permanent target for insults.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “like a warrior overcome with wine.” The Hebrew verb רוּן (run, “overcome”) occurs only here in the OT. The phrase “overcome with wine” could picture a drunken warrior controlled by his emotions and passions (as in the present translation), or it could refer to a warrior who awakes from a drunken stupor.

verses.zh: 并且他弃掉约瑟的帐棚，不拣选以法莲支派，
verses.en: He rejected the tent of Joseph;he did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.

verses.zh: 却拣选犹大支派―他所喜爱的锡安山；
verses.en: He chose the tribe of Judahand Mount Zion, which he loves.

verses.zh: 盖造他的圣所，好像高峰，又像他建立永存之地；
verses.en: He made his sanctuary as enduring as the heavens above,[NOTE:1] as secure as the earth, which he established permanently.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “a permanent reproach he made them.”

Heb “and he built like the exalting [ones] his sanctuary.” The phrase כְּמוֹ־רָמִים (kemo ramim, “like the exalting [ones]”) is a poetic form of the comparative preposition followed by a participial form of the verb רוּם (rum, “be exalted”). The text should be emended to כִּמְרֹמִים (kimromim, “like the [heavenly] heights”). See Ps 148:1, where “heights” refers to the heavens above.

The MT has "like the high heavens." The Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE
(BDB 926, KB 1202) has a wide semantical field. KB lists several options.

- to be high above

- reach high

- be exalted

- rise up, go up

- referring to being lifted onto a high rock

- high

- loud

- tall

- haughty

- exalted ones (i.e., heavenly beings)

NET Bible suggests an emendation to "like heavenly heights," from usage in Ps. 148:1. The
PARTICIPLE is parallel to "Mount Zion" in the line above (v. 68b) and therefore, refers to
the temple on Mt. Moriah. This strophe focuses on royal imagery from

- David's reign

- David's capture of Jebus and preparing for the building of the temple by Solomon

Obviously this psalm has gone through an editorial process of many years.

verses.zh: 又拣选他的仆人大卫，从羊圈中将他召来，
verses.en: He chose David, his servant,and took him from the sheepfolds.

verses.zh: 叫他不再跟从那些带奶的母羊，为要牧养自己的百姓雅各和自己的产业以色列。
verses.en: He took him away from following the mother sheep,[NOTE:1] and made him the shepherd of Jacob, his people,and of Israel, his chosen nation.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “like the earth, [which] he established permanently.” The feminine singular suffix on the Hebrew verb יָסַד (yasad, “to establish”) refers to the grammatically feminine noun “earth.”
Heb “from after the ewes he brought him.”

verses.zh: 于是，他按心中的纯正牧养他们，用手中的巧妙引导他们。
verses.en: David[NOTE:1] cared for them with pure motives;[NOTE:2] he led them with skill.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “to shepherd Jacob, his people, and Israel, his inheritance.”
Heb “He”; the referent (David, God’s chosen king, mentioned in v. 70) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and he shepherded them according to the integrity of his heart.”

- Notice the different names for Deity used.

- YHWH, vv. 4, 21

- El, vv. 7, 8, 18, 19, 35, 41

- Most High, vv. 17, 35

- Adon, v. 65

So many titles and personal PRONOUNS. Deity was faithful; the covenant people were not!

Also, notice three Divine names appear in v. 35, which shows some overlap, yet with distinction.
